title: Security Solution Status Check
unit: CS-ICT251101 Monitor and Report Cyber Threats

parts.html:
At the end of this session, you should be able to:

  1. Explain why a monitoring analyst checks the security solutions themselves, not only their alerts.
  2. Check whether the required enterprise security solutions are installed on every host, and find coverage gaps (PC 2.1).
  3. Check whether each security solution is operational against the SOP checks (PC 2.2).
  4. Check whether a security solution can clean or delete a detected issue, from its policy and the threat type (PC 2.3).
  5. Run the full status check on a Windows workstation with PowerShell and report what fails.

Every alert you handled on Days 5 and 6 came from a security solution. If that solution is missing, stopped, out of date or not allowed to act, there is no alert at all, and a quiet console looks exactly like a safe network. Element 2 of the Competency Standards asks three questions about every security solution. In the lab you follow SOC-SOP-03 Security Solution Status Check (~/day7/soc_status_sop.txt).

  1. Is it installed? (PC 2.1)
  2. Is it operational? (PC 2.2)
  3. Can it clean or delete the issue? (PC 2.3)

The same three questions apply to every security solution in the Range of Variables: anti-virus, common firewall, threat intelligence, TDR, WAF, IDS, IPS, DLP, OT/ICS/SCADA security, IoT security, EDR/MDR, SIEM, SOAR and XDR. Today we practise on the three that sit on every computer: anti-virus (Microsoft Defender), EDR (CrowdStrike Falcon) and the SIEM agent (Wazuh).

The SOP says which enterprise security solutions every kind of host must have. Compare the organization's list of computers (the endpoint inventory) with what the security console reports.

Host TypeAV (Defender)EDR (Falcon)SIEM Agent (Wazuh)
Windows server or workstationrequiredrequiredrequired
Linux server—requiredrequired
Tier 3 test PC (isolated VLAN)requirednot requiredrequired
NOTE — The host the console has never seen
A computer that was never enrolled does not appear in the console as "Not installed": it does not appear at all. Always start from the endpoint inventory and look for every host in the console report. Counting the lines of both files (wc -l) is a quick first check.

Installed is not the same as working. A solution is operational only when every check passes:

Check (SOC-SOP-03)Passes WhenWhere You See It
B1 ServiceRunningGet-Service
B2 Real-time protectionOn (anti-virus)Get-MpComputerStatus
B3 Check-inNo more than 60 minutes agoConsole health export; agent log
B4 ContentSignatures dated within 3 daysAntivirusSignatureLastUpdated
B5 VersionAt or above the minimum supported versionConsole health export
B6 Tamper protectionOnIsTamperProtected
TIP — "Running" does not mean "working"
A Wazuh agent service can be Running while the agent has lost its connection to the SIEM manager: nothing reaches the SOC. Read the last lines of its log (ossec.log): "Keep alive acknowledged" means connected; "Lost connection with manager" means the SOC is blind on that computer.

parts.h: 4. Can It Clean or Delete the Issue? (PC 2.3)
parts.html:
A solution can detect a threat and still be unable to remove it, because of its policy or the kind of threat. Microsoft Defender's policy (Get-MpPreference) sets a default action for each severity:

Action CodeMeaning
1Clean
2Quarantine
3Remove
6Allow
8User defined
9No action
10Block
RuleMeaning
C1 Action codeCan clean or delete only with action 1, 2, 3 or 10 for the threat's severity
C2 ExclusionA folder in ExclusionPath is not scanned; user folders (Downloads, Desktop, Temp, Documents) must never be excluded
C3 Detect onlyEDR in "Detect only" mode raises alerts but cannot stop or remove anything; required mode is "Prevent"
C4 Re-imageRansomware, rootkits and boot-sector infections: the host is rebuilt by IT, even if the file was deleted

Actions in the Range of Variables

ActionMeaning
FailedThe solution tried and could not act: report it
CleanMalicious code removed, file kept
DeleteFile removed
QuarantineFile moved to a safe, locked place
BlockedStopped before it could run or connect
Re-imageHost rebuilt from a clean image

• A missing required solution or a host never enrolled (coverage gap)
  • A failed operational check, with the check code (B1–B6)
  • A policy that cannot clean: the action code, the exclusion or the detect-only mode
  • A detection that needs a re-image
  • Report to the Shift Lead. Level I does not change policies or uninstall anything.

TermMeaning
Enterprise security solutionSecurity software managed centrally for the whole organization
Agent / sensorThe small program on each computer that reports to the console
Coverage gapA host without a required security solution
Check-in / keep-aliveThe regular "I am alive" message from an agent to its console or manager
Tamper protectionA setting that stops users and malware from switching security off
ExclusionA folder, file or process the solution is told to ignore
Detect only modeThe solution watches and alerts but never blocks or removes
Re-imageWiping a computer and reinstalling it from a known clean image
